newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates down, spots mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates down, spots mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Monday mainly because of a weak performance by the domestic A share indices, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded three-day contract rose to 4.15 percent from 3.11 percent on last Friday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 2.24 million lots from 1.16 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Both the Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets fell sharply on Monday, leaving a negative impression on the repurchase market, traders said.
The weak performance of domestic currency A shares sharply reduced fund demand on the repo market and forced most institutions to stick to the sidelines, they said.
"The A share falls dampened the repo market sentiment and pushed most of the contracts down," said one trader.
Traders said they expected the rates to consolidate around the current low levels in the next few days due to a lack of positive market-moving news.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Monday mainly due to an injection of funds by some short-term investors on to the spot market in the wake of the A share weakness, traders said.
The most actively traded seven-year bond that matures in November 2003 rose to 98.25 yuan from 98.00 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market soared to 820,281 lots from 206,084 lots.
Traders said fresh money was seen flowing into the market on Monday -- a major factor boosting both prices and volume.
Prices were likely to rise further in the next few days if A shares continued their weak run, they said.
